literal: Among joys joy it will yield, hostility called among sorrows sorrow if destroyed.
translation: If the greatest of sorrows called hostility is destroyed, it will yield the greatest of joys.
modern: இகல் என்று சொல்லப்படும் மிகப்பெரிய துன்பம் ஒருவனை விட்டு ஒழிந்தால் அது அவனுக்கு எல்லா இன்பங்களிலும் சிறந்த இன்பத்தைத் தரும்.
explanation: This couplet describes hostility as the worst possible sorrow a person can experience. If one can completely eradicate this destructive feeling, the result is not merely peace, but the highest form of joy. The poet uses the contrasting phrases 'sorrow of sorrows' and 'joy of joys' to emphasize how deeply hostility affects human happiness.
